THEY WILL HAVE THE CREW REST FOR ABOUT 48 HOURS BEFOR NASA's rollout of the Artemis II rocket complete after wind delay Updated: 4:27 PM EDT Mar 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ NASA's Artemis II rocket rollout is complete after a wind delay overnight, according to officials.The process was supposed to start at 8 p.m. on Thursday, moving the rocket from the Vehicle Assembly Building to the launch pad at Kennedy Space Center. Officials hope for liftoff between April 1 and April 6, following the resolution of an issue with the flow of helium in the rocket's upper stage.The rollout process, which could take between eight and 12 hours, marks the second time NASA has undertaken this procedure with Artemis II.NASA has confirmed that the helium issue has been fixed, and the Artemis II team is currently in quarantine in Houston. During a recent news conference, NASA officials said, "Again, while I am comfortable and the agency is comfortable with targeting April 1st as our first opportunity. Just keep in mind we still have work to go. There are still things that need to be done within the VAB and out at the pad. And as always, we'll always be guided by what the hardware is telling us, and we will launch when we're ready." CAPE CANAVERAL, FL —NASA's Artemis II rocket rollout is complete after a wind delay overnight, according to officials.The process was supposed to start at 8 p.m. on Thursday, moving the rocket from the Vehicle Assembly Building to the launch pad at Kennedy Space Center. Officials hope for liftoff between April 1 and April 6, following the resolution of an issue with the flow of helium in the rocket's upper stage. The new data covers population changes from July 1, 2024, to July 1, 2025. Nationwide, the population growth rate has slowed due to declines in net international migration.The 2025 Vintage estimates released Thursday detail population shifts for metropolitan areas and counties. The data includes population estimates plus the components of change, including birth, death and migration patterns.The metropolitan area with the largest growth from 2024 to 2025 was Ocala, Florida, at 3.4%. Metropolitan statistical areas are defined by the Census Bureau as having at least one urban area of 50,000 or more people.Other places in the top 10 include areas in South Carolina, other parts of Florida and North Carolina. South Carolina and North Carolina had the highest statewide population growth in 2025.While many parts of the U.S. saw growth, many large cities and more populous counties mimicked the national trend of a slowing growth rate caused by a decline in the net international migration rate.Other data points that contribute to population growth in a given county or metropolitan area include domestic migration, births and deaths. More people have typically left metropolitan areas and the most populated counties than moved to them in the past two years. The rate of natural change, which is the difference in the number of births and deaths, has also remained the same in the past two years across different geographies. Trends of more people being born in highly populated areas continued in 2025.Search the maps below to see how populations in metropolitan areas, micropolitan areas and counties changed last year. WASHINGTON —Populations are growing at a faster rate in the southeastern United States, according to new data released by the U.S. Census Bureau on Thursday. The new data covers population changes from July 1, 2024, to July 1, 2025. Nationwide, the population growth rate has slowed due to declines in net international migration. The 2025 Vintage estimates released Thursday detail population shifts for metropolitan areas and counties. The data includes population estimates plus the components of change, including birth, death and migration patterns. The metropolitan area with the largest growth from 2024 to 2025 was Ocala, Florida, at 3.4%. Metropolitan statistical areas are defined by the Census Bureau as having at least one urban area of 50,000 or more people.Other places in the top 10 include areas in South Carolina, other parts of Florida and North Carolina. South Carolina and North Carolina had the highest statewide population growth in 2025. While many parts of the U.S. saw growth, many large cities and more populous counties mimicked the national trend of a slowing growth rate caused by a decline in the net international migration rate. Other data points that contribute to population growth in a given county or metropolitan area include domestic migration, births and deaths. More people have typically left metropolitan areas and the most populated counties than moved to them in the past two years. The rate of natural change, which is the difference in the number of births and deaths, has also remained the same in the past two years across different geographies.
